yellow_fever_or_health_rule: Government entry guidance says visitors should carry a yellow-fever vaccination card. The detailed GID rule requires a certificate for travellers aged 9 months or over arriving from a yellow-fever-risk country or transiting for more than 12 hours through an airport in a risk country. Bangladesh itself is not a yellow-fever-risk country; check itinerary and current health notices. The February 2026 High Commission PDF also contains a PCR-within-72-hours statement that appears stale and is not treated as a current requirement.
transit_rule: Direct transit within the airport precinct for up to 48 hours uses a transit pass and does not require a visa. Indirect transit beyond 48 hours requires a single-entry visa valid up to seven days, with onward ticket and assured admission to the next country. This is the general transit rule, separate from the Commonwealth visitor exemption.
application_channel: No visa or entry-clearance application is required for Commonwealth citizens, including Bangladesh, for visitor stays up to 90 days under the 2026 policy. Enter through a recognized port with a valid travel document and visible means of sustenance; immigration screening applies.
application_fee: No visa fee; Securiport airport fee D1,000 (~US$20) is separate and not mandated by GID; verify collection.
processing_time: Not applicable to visa-exempt entry; no advance visa processing.
required_documents: Valid passport or travel document|Return or onward ticket|Evidence of sufficient means of sustenance|Yellow-fever certificate if arriving from a risk country or transiting more than 12 hours through a risk-country airport|Accommodation or host details where applicable|Arrival card and biometric enrolment at entry
official_immigration_source_name: Government of The Gambia — Immigration and Visa Information
review_notes: The Government of The Gambia immigration page and the February 2026 Gambia High Commission policy state that Commonwealth citizens are visa-exempt for up to 90 days. Bangladesh is a Commonwealth member (joined 1972), and the policy applies to nationals with valid travel documents without limiting the exemption to diplomatic or official passports. The older Gambia Immigration Department Visa Services page still lists Bangladesh under countries requiring both visa and clearance; this is a live but older contradictory nationality list. The newer Government and High Commission policy is treated as controlling, while the GID page is retained as a conflicting source requiring correction/confirmation. The 15 March 2025 bilateral agreement is only for diplomatic and official passports and is not relied upon for ordinary passports. No visa fee applies to the Commonwealth exemption. The February 2026 policy separately lists a Securiport airport fee of D1,000 (about USD20) for most passengers and states that it is not mandated by GID; confirm current collection. Commonwealth visitor entry is up to 90 days, subject to recognized-port entry, visible means of sustenance and immigration screening. The policy describes arrival biometric enrolment (fingerprints, iris and passport data page).
